alternatives.labelRationale: Five anatomy, infection, health-psychology, ethics and neurobiology courses are replaced by advanced calculus, linear algebra, systems, optimisation and neural-network study, creating a quantitative drug-action curriculum without claiming pharmacometrics or pharmaceutical chemistry.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. Functional Anatomy, Infection & Immunity, Medical & Health Psychology, Ethics and Neurobiology are replaced by Advanced Calculus, Linear Algebra, Linear Systems, Optimization Methods in AI and Neural Networks & Deep Learning. The resulting choice shifts from biological systems, medicine use and patient context to quantitative modelling and data-driven treatment evidence.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass the evidence, course-content, schedule and 30-EC distinctness gates. A third patient-facing pharmacy route is not defensible because the workbook lacks pharmaceutics and formulation, dispensing and product care, clinical pharmacy, medication review, dosage practice, patient counselling, pharmacy law/regulation and supervised pharmacist practice. General health psychology and ethics complement the first route but cannot be expanded into a pharmacy-practice curriculum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce biological foundations for medicine study; UCR remains a general life/health gateway rather than a pharmacy introduction.
Both address cellular and molecular mechanisms relevant to biological medicines; UCR does not reproduce pharmaceutical biotechnology or product development.
Both address endocrine physiology; UCR studies integrated human physiology rather than the complete pharmacy disease block.
Both involve experimental investigation; UCR supplies a broad life-science laboratory rather than medicine-specific pharmaceutical research.
UCR molecular pathology and genetics directly address neoplasia and cancer mechanisms, but not oncology pharmacotherapy as a complete block.
Both directly study infection and immune defence; the external course integrates these subjects with pharmacy.
Both address cardiovascular pathophysiology; UCR does not reproduce pharmaceutical treatment training.
Both address neurobiology and neurological disorders; UCR does not claim the external therapeutic or pharmacy framing.
The pharmacy skin-disease block remains visible; UCR has no dedicated dermatology or dermatological-pharmacy course.
UCR Infection & Immunity is aligned once and does not duplicate the external autoimmune-disease block.
UCR Neurobiology and Pharmacology are each aligned once; there is no dedicated psychopharmacology course.
Both directly study drug targets, mechanisms, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic use and toxicity.
UCR Pharmacology addresses pharmacokinetics once; the external dedicated kinetics block remains separately visible.
The integrated pharmacy therapy block remains visible; UCR disease and pharmacology courses do not reproduce clinical pharmacotherapy.
UCR does not offer dedicated medicine-administration or dosage-form training.
UCR Biochemistry does not replace pharmaceutical chemistry.
The workbook lacks formulation, quality, dispensing and pharmaceutical product-care training.
The genuine 7.5-EC external profiling space is preserved without invented content.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives combine molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, disease mechanisms, laboratory work, health behaviour and quantitative research. They do not reproduce pharmaceutical chemistry, formulation, product care, dispensing, clinical pharmacy, patient counselling, pharmacy regulation or supervised pharmacist practice, and therefore represent related biomedical routes rather than a full Pharmacy curriculum.
